title: CUDA lib overlay huntlog
content:
Quick summary:
- Intermittent GPU OOMs on a small number of hosts running model A (1x A100-40GB). Not correlated with sustained high GPU util. Suspect mixed CUDA/libcuda library versions in container vs host (overlayed libs), sometimes triggered after kubelet restart / docker upgrade.

Symptoms observed:
- Process dies with CUDA out of memory even when nvidia-smi shows 2–3GB free.
- Logs show: "CUDA error: out of memory" followed by stack in c10::cuda::(anonymous)
- /var/log/syslog shows driver unload messages shortly before some failures.
- Reproduced once by forcing rapid create/destroy of contexts across processes.

Environment matrix (not exhaustive):
- Host driver: 535.113.01 (prod fleet mix: some 535.x, some 525.x)
- Host kernel: 6.1.0-29 and 5.15 variants across pool
- Container base images: ubuntu22.04 + nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime or slim python images with pip wheels
- Torch wheels in use: torch 2.2.* built for cu121 (in most images) but some older images still have cu117 wheels or binary-built libs (mixed)
- nvidia-container-toolkit: 1.14.0 installed on some hosts, older on others

Commands & quick checks I ran (timestamps approximate):
1) Validate driver/status
- nvidia-smi -q | head -n 20  # driver load / device health
- kernel module list: lsmod | grep nvidia
- journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --no-pager | tail -n 200

2) Container inspection (from host)
- docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime nvidia-smi
- docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint=sh my-image -c 'ldd $(python -c "import torch;print(torch._C.__file__)") | grep cuda || true'
- docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint=sh my-image -c 'ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart* || true'

Observed oddities:
- In one image, libcuda.so.1 inside container was a symlink to an older ABI path (/usr/local/cuda-11.7/lib64/libcuda.so.1) while host driver was 535 expecting cu121 runtime.
- ldd on torch _C extension showed unresolved libcuda symbols in that container (warning lines).
- docker image had /usr/local/cuda present from buildkit cache even though base was supposed to be runtime-only; likely leftover from a multi-stage build.

Error log snippets captured:
- "RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory. tried to allocate 2147483648 bytes"
- "E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:... CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT" (seen in older TF container builds)
- host syslog:
  Mar 5 02:13:12 node-42 kernel: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: failed to initialize
  Mar 5 02:13:12 node-42 kernel: NVRM: The NVIDIA probe routine was not called for 1 device(s).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Library overlay mismatch: container has leftover CUDA libs (cuda-11.x) that shadow host-provided libcuda, creating ABI mismatch and unexpected allocation behavior.
2) Driver module flapping on host (kubelet/docker restarts) leaves device in a state where user-space libs think some memory is free but driver has not reclaimed pages.
3) Torch wheel / cuda runtime mismatch: some wheels compiled against different CUDA ABI cause different allocation paths and KV cache behavior -> leak/fragmentation.
4) MPS or nvidia-persistenced not running or failing, leading to context thrash under multi-tenancy causing temporary OOMs.

Investigations done vs next steps:
- Done: Grep for libcuda in image layers: docker save -> tar -> grepping layer contents. Found /usr/local/cuda leftover in 3 images.
- Done: Rebuilt image with explicit rm -rf /usr/local/cuda* in final stage --> suspect fix on one host for 48h no repro.
- Done: Forced host driver downgrade to 525 on a test node -> repro rate reduced (only one observed in 72h) but not conclusive.

Next things to try (practical checklist):
- Create a small repro container image (minimal python + torch cu121) and instrument allocation patterns to reproduce quickly:
  * python snippet: allocate random tensors of various shapes in a loop, force gc, allocate a big tensor to reproduce OOM.
  * run 10 parallel processes to mimic multi-tenant context churn.
- Add runtime check at container startup to fail fast if any libcuda.so.* exists in container (exit 1 + logs):
  if ls /usr/local/cuda* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* 2>/dev/null; then echo "container-embedded-cuda-libs"; exit 15; fi
- Add kube node e2e job that restarts kubelet + docker and runs the repro workload to try reproduce module flapping effects.
- Enable more verbose driver logs on suspect hosts: NVRM_LOG_LEVEL=5 and collect dmesg + nvidia-smi --query to correlate times.
- Try building torch wheel from source in a clean cu121 chroot and run that in suspect images to rule out pip wheel mismatch.
- Check nvidia-container-toolkit versions across fleet and standardize to >=1.13 recommended.

Quick repro (notes to self) - python sketch:
- pip install torch==2.2.0+cu121 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html
- script (loop_alloc.py):
  import torch, gc, time
  def burn(i):
    for _ in range(100):
      x = torch.randn(1024, 1024, device='cuda')*0.1
      del x
      gc.collect()
    time.sleep(0.5)
  if __name__=='__main__':
    import multiprocessing as mp
    ps = [mp.Process(target=burn, args=(i,)) for i in range(6)]
    for p in ps: p.start()
    for p in ps: p.join()
  # then allocate: torch.empty(10000, 10000, device='cuda') to force OOM

Notes / odd leads to chase later:
- Found a host where ldconfig cache included /usr/local/cuda-11.7 earlier in the boot path — why? some legacy rpm package installs. Need to check image-builder scripts for copy operations.
- hypothesis: buildkite agent on some images used host-mounted /usr/local/cuda during build step and accidentally embedded symlinks in final image layer. Need to audit build scripts.

Unresolved questions:
- Why does nvidia-smi sometimes show free mem but process still OOMs? (fragmentation vs driver bookkeeping mismatch)
- Are there any race conditions in our runtime that cause contexts to be created/destroyed in a tight loop (e.g., healthcheck podrunner?)

Immediate mitigations deployed (low-risk):
- Add container-entrypoint check to fail images that contain embedded CUDA libs (rollout to canary).
- Add node-monitoring alert for nvidia kernel module reloads.

References & tickets to follow up:
- GHD-1284 (investigations and canary rollout)
- PR: serving-runtime#402 (adds entrypoint lib check)

Notes to self: keep the huntlog chronological and dump capture files to s3://redwood-debug/gpu-oom/cuda-lib-overlay/ with node/date tags. When reproducing, record: docker image id, kernel version, driver version, output of: uname -a; nvidia-smi -q; lsmod | grep nvidia; ldd $(python -c 'import torch;print(torch._C.__file__)')

End of scratchpad - still rough. Revisit after running kubelet restart matrix tests.
